prerequisites: Signed-out browser context with no app account.
A private scratch directory outside the instance for the extracted standalone edition.
scenarios.expected: The reader can identify the supported build and content and reach the intended local or external support path. An older or unknown edition does not silently switch to latest, and an external-site failure leaves local reading usable.
scenarios.actual: 2 recorded steps passed for this role on 3fa407e3. Signed out, /documentation/versions-and-support opened with no app API requests. Download standalone edition gave openlaw-documentation.tar.gz, and Open standalone edition served /documentation-export/index.html. The archive was extracted outside the instance. In an offline browser context from file://, the index, the Reference and troubleshooting section and the support article read with JavaScript and without it. Without JavaScript the index showed "Search requires JavaScript." All internal link targets in the reviewed versions-and-support and troubleshooting bytes opened in the formal reader.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the source-review author; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.

The lab Help and formal readers serve the article bytes committed at 3fa407e3, which differ from the reviewed corrected bytes. Steps followed the reviewed bytes against the app. Reader checks prove the routes, headings and UI behavior; link checks opened every internal link of the reviewed bytes in the bundled formal reader.
The admin lab is shared with other DOC-029 agents. The walkthrough created only records named DOC-029 support ... and changed no organisation settings.

Two earlier recorded attempts (walkthrough-r1-attempt1.json, walkthrough-r1-attempt2.json) each had one reviewer harness fault and are kept with their disposition. Exploratory probes and development runs before them are not evidence.

Supported app showed a recorded build (0.0.1 / 7f7e917a...), so the Not yet verified value and the Working changes marker were not observed. The Unverified article badge was not shown; the Validation in progress badge was.
The offline check used an offline browser context and file:// loading of the extracted export while the lab kept running. It did not stop the shared lab.
The external failure was a browser-blocked github.com request, not a real outage. No GitHub issue was opened.
The administrator screenshot shows the lab's served article bytes, whose example section name differs from the reviewed bytes.
